citation.title: A Parametric Level Set Method for Topology Optimization based on Deep Neural Network (DNN)
citation.version_coded: arXiv PDF (version not stated in downloaded text)

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: For the MBB beam, DNN level-set designs with one or two hidden layers attain compliance close to the SIMP benchmark value of 33.48.
claim.key_phrase: quite close with the benchmark solution
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: No comparative runtime or speed-up is reported.
claim.alternatives: Section 4.2/Figures 15 and 18: two- or three-layer DNN compliance is reported about 3.5% below SIMP; Figure 19 reports other compliance values.

baseline.problem_size: MBB: 200 x 100 elements (Section 4.1); short cantilever: 100 x 100 elements (Section 4.2)
baseline.quality_metric: Structural compliance, computed with FEM in the DNN optimization (Section 3.2; Section 4)
baseline.quality_gap: MBB SIMP compliance 33.48 (Figure 11), DNN designs described as close (Section 4.1); short cantilever DNN with two or three layers about 3.5% below SIMP (Section 4.2)

R1.evidence: Section 4 compares compliance, without a runtime comparison.

R2.evidence: Section 4 compares compliance only; classical solver speed is not an outcome.

R3.evidence: Abstract and Sections 4-5 make no speed claim for the proposed method.

R4.evidence: Sections 3.2 and 4 use FEM compliance for the produced designs, but Section 4 does not count infeasible designs or report achieved volume for every output.

reporting.n_test_cases: 2 benchmark problems (Sections 4.1-4.2); multiple architectures per problem (Figures 12 and 19)

notes: The network is optimized separately for each design; there is no offline training set for inference. The SIMP comparison is quantitative design quality, placing the record in the secondary quality stratum.
